sections.h2: Railways spent ₹107 for every ₹100 earned in 2021-22

chart.title: The operating ratio has stayed near 98% since 2018-19, peaking at 107%
chart.sub: Working expenses as a share of traffic receipts, %.

sections.means: The ratio has stayed above 96% every year since 2016-17, and reached 107% in 2021-22.
sections.todo: Track each service's cost against its revenue so the ratio is managed deliberately, not only reported annually.

sections.h2: Freight rates rose 91% in a decade while passenger fares rose 28%

chart.title: Freight rates grew far faster than passenger fares over 2009 to 2019
chart.sub: Change in freight rates and passenger fares, 2009 to 2019, %.

sections.means: Freight is funding passenger losses that are classed as social obligations rather than commercial failures.
sections.todo: Rationalise freight rates through direct budgetary support rather than continued cross-subsidy, as the Hindu Centre analysis proposes.

sections.h2: A 2015 committee asked for train-wise costing; a 2024 reply shows it is still missing

chart.title: Nine years on, Railways still cannot say whether Vande Bharat makes money
events: Debroy Committee finds the accounting system cannot say what it costs to run a train.
RTI reply on Vande Bharat: "train-wise portability is not maintained".

sections.means: The 2015 committee said Railways could not cost individual trains, and the 2024 RTI reply shows that is still true.
sections.todo: Adopt the committee's accrual, double-entry accounting so each train's cost and viability can be determined.
